channel.title: The Awesome Ledger — awesome-zsh-plugins
channel.description: New entries across the GitHub awesome ecosystem, diffed nightly.

item.title: passwords — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Passwords and 2FA (TOTP) codes from Apple Passwords / iCloud Keychain, straight from zsh, without leaking them into history, scrollback, ps, or clipboard managers.

item.title: omz-plus — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: pre-processes the builtin Oh-My-Zsh variables you're already using. By sourcing OMZ Plus! right before you source Oh-My-Zsh, it detects git-hosted plugins, handles cloning and symlinking, and then scrubs those variables back to the basics so that they are ready for oh-my-zsh to use

item.title: ltree — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Works like the tree command, but truncates large directories by printing the first n files and summarizing the rest as ... m more files.

item.title: aurora — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Minimal theme with the Dracula color palette. Includes decorators for username@hostname, current directory and git status.

item.title: zsh-editor-keys — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Brings modern GUI editor keybindings to ZSH including Shift+Arrow char/subword/multi-line selection, cross-platform OS clipboard Cmd+C/X/V and Ctrl+Shift+C/X/V, Alt+A select all, Alt+Z undo/redo, and Shift+Enter newlines.

item.title: zsh-dropdown — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Adds a flicker-free, prefix-only live completion dropdown for ZSH using DEC Mode 2026 synchronized redraws, automatic 24-bit/256-color themes, and ZSH 5.9 zasync self-healing.

item.title: wslpath — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Convert a Windows path on the WSL ZSH command line by pressing Tab. Pasting or dragging a path into the terminal does not change it. The plugin uses WSL's wslpath and only replaces the path if the file or directory exists.

item.title: fzf-unified — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A single managed source of truth for everything fzf inside ZSH: shell integration (Ctrl-T / Alt-C), history search (Ctrl-R), ripgrep live grep (Ctrl-G), Tab completion (fzf-tab, vendored) and the Up/Down arrow policy — one plugin instead of several loosely-coupled ones fighting over the same keybindings.

item.title: apathy — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A terminal-to-agent zsh CLI that converts your pasted LLM prompts into actual invokes of harnesses like OpenCode, Claude Code and more. It manages to tell the difference between commands meant for your terminal, and prompts meant for your agent, as well as retain what you previously typed in your terminal.

item.title: shellsense (ThePubDoc) — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: IDE-style autocomplete for your terminal. Type a command and a list of what can come next opens under the word you are typing: subcommands, options, git branches, npm scripts, files and folders, each with a short description. Pick one with the arrow keys or keep typing to narrow the list.

item.title: hexagon — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Minimalist ZSH theme based on geometry.

item.title: copylast — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Reads the last command's output straight out of tmux's scrollback, so it's instant and you get exactly what you saw.

item.title: zest — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Fig-style autocomplete popup for macOS. Shows subcommands, options, git branches and files with descriptions under the cursor in Terminal.app, VS Code and Cursor. Specs for 1,500 commands; new ones are a YAML file.

item.title: git-sweep — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Small ZSH plugin for cleaning up Git branches and worktrees, with protected branch patterns, dry-run previews, optional interactive selection, and explicit remote cleanup.

item.title: worktrunk-herdr — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: glues Worktrunk (wt), AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi) and herdr together.

item.title: gui-detach — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Returns the prompt in interactive ZSH when a GUI app is launched on Linux, and leaves CLI tools in the foreground.

item.title: slowrc — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Profiles your ZSH startup line by line, shows which lines of your .zshrc cost the most, and safely fixes the slow ones.

item.title: listview — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Lightweight, zero-dependency ZSH plugin inspired by PowerShell's PSReadLine ListView. Displays real-time, non-intrusive unique history suggestions below your prompt as you type, navigatable using arrow keys.

item.title: Cue — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Adds IDE-style command, option, and path suggestions to ZSH in a native macOS popup.

item.title: speedrunner — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Speeds up the start of Python, Ruby, PHP and Node CLIs by forking them from a preloaded daemon. Its ZSH hook starts the daemon while you type the command name.

item.title: walh-shell — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A fast, modern, and extensible Zsh (and Bash) plugin for instant terminal color theme switching that lets you instantly change your terminal’s color scheme with a single command.

item.title: sprout — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Turn a Jira ticket into a clean git branch. One command. A short, descriptive name. Zero copy-pasting.

item.title: claude-guard — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: checks your egress IP before Claude Code starts. If the IP that claude.ai sees is not on your allowlist, claude stops and asks before it connects.

item.title: oops — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Copies the last command and its output to the clipboard as a Markdown code block, with API keys and other secrets masked. Works in ZSH and bash. Installed as a Ruby gem (Ruby 3.3 or later).

item.title: fasd — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A command-line productivity booster. Fasd offers quick access to files and directories for POSIX shells. It is inspired by tools like autojump, z and v. Fasd keeps track of files and directories you have accessed, so that you can quickly reference them in the command line.

item.title: claude-code — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Adds ask and explain commands plus Ctrl+X (rewrite a natural-language request into a command, in place) and Alt+E (explain the typed command) widgets, built on the Claude Code CLI with tools and MCP servers disabled.

item.title: utm — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Adds a single utm command on top of utmctl, the command line tool that ships with UTM, with tab completion for subcommands, virtual machine names and snapshot names, and a --wait that utmctl does not have.

item.title: tmux-inside — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A drop-in replacement for the oh-my-zsh tmux plugin that makes the tmux aliases work from inside a tmux session: instead of trying to nest a session (which tmux refuses), they switch to the target session, creating it detached in the current directory if needed.

item.title: tab-start — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: adds starter entries to ZSH completion when you press TAB at a blank prompt. Uses fzf-tab to render those entries and provides grouping, fuzzy search, and selection.

item.title: sf-shortcuts — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Short, predictable commands for the Salesforce CLI (sf), with tab completion for Apex classes, components (aura/lightning) and orgs.

item.title: curl-edit — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Automatically open pasted cURL commands in an editor before executing them.

item.title: claude-sandbox — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Points CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at a throwaway directory, so everything Claude Code reads and writes (settings, plugins, skills, history, credentials) stays inside that sandbox. Leave it, delete it, and your real setup is exactly as you left it.

item.title: aws-login — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Provides an aws-login command that starts an AWS session that only the current terminal and its child processes can use.

item.title: SparkleBIOS — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Draws a retro 1995 PC BIOS boot screen with real system facts and cached health checks when a new ZSH session starts.

item.title: friesent — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Minimalist theme with decorators for username@host, an arrow that turns green or red based on the last command's exit status, the current directory, and git branch/status when inside a repository.

item.title: shtab — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Automatically generate shell tab completion scripts for Python CLI apps, supports zsh, bash and tcsh.

item.title: suvadu — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Shell history in local SQLite with directory, exit code and AI agent commands, with a ZSH widget for Ctrl+R and Up-arrow recall.

item.title: spotify-now — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Shows the track Spotify is playing in your prompt, in a green box with animated equalizer bars. Works on macOS and Linux.

item.title: rtfm — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Puts the manual under your thumb. Hit Tab, fuzzy-filter what you need, read the description, insert the token, without leaving the line, and without guessing.

item.title: ai-cli — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Describe what you want in plain English and get a shell command back, ready to edit or run. Claude writes the command, or a model you run yourself through Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible server; nothing runs until you press Enter. Type a request and press Ctrl-O, or run ai <request>.

item.title: zdx-suite — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Interactive, fzf-powered developer workflows and a custom plugin loader for ZSH, built for oh-my-zsh.

item.title: rfig — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Adds command completion menus and directory-scoped history autosuggestions to ZSH, Bash and Fish on macOS and Linux. Written in Rust.

item.title: pratchett — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Displays a random Terry Pratchett quote from the Discworld novels, copied verbatim from Wikiquote. Includes a quote of the day, filtering by book, search, and tab completion; DEATH delivers his own lines if cowsay is installed.

item.title: partner — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Theme where every git branch hatches its own pet. Your pet evolves as you commit on the branch, so your prompt shows how much work you've put in. Includes decorators for git branch and current directory.

item.title: ls-branch-label — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Shows the current git branch next to repository directories when you run a plain ls.

item.title: debian — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Provides Debian-related aliases and functions. Forked from the oh-my-zsh debian plugin.

item.title: certview — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Fast inspection and verification of X.509 certificates, CSRs, and cryptographic keys (RSA, ECC, Ed25519) in both PEM and DER formats.

item.title: zshrs-fasd — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Native zshrs plugin for fasd.

item.title: vercel — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Tab completion for the Vercel CLI.

item.title: cad0p — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: One-line theme with a 24-hour clock, user@host, current directory and git status decorations. Based on the geoffgarside theme from Oh-My-ZSH.
